questions.explanation: Regression testing is performed after developers make changes to an application. It reruns a number of test cases and compares the results to baseline results. Orthogonal array testing is a method for generating test cases based on statistical analysis. Pattern testing uses records of past software bugs to inform the analysis. Matrix testing develops a matrix of all possible inputs and outputs to inform the test plan.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Orthogonal array testing uses statistical analysis to generate test cases. It isn't about rerunning tests after a change and comparing the results to a baseline.
Incorrect. Pattern testing uses records of past software bugs to guide the analysis. It doesn't rerun scenarios against a baseline after each change.
Incorrect. Matrix testing builds a matrix of all possible inputs and outputs to shape the test plan. It's a planning method, not repeated retesting against a baseline.
Correct. Regression testing is done after developers change the software. It reruns many test cases and compares the results with baseline results to confirm nothing has broken.

questions.stem: Haley is reviewing code created by her organization for its possible exposure to web application vulnerabilities. Which one of the following conditions may make an application most vulnerable to a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack?
questions.explanation: Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks may take advantage of the use of reflected input in a web application where input provided by one user is displayed to another user. Input validation is a control used to prevent XSS attacks. XSS does not require an unpatched server or any firewall rules beyond those permitting access to the web application.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Input validation is a defense against XSS, not a weakness. It filters or rejects script content before the application processes or displays it.
Correct. XSS exploits reflected input, where input supplied by one user is displayed to another user without sanitization, so the injected script runs in the victim's browser.
Incorrect. XSS is a flaw in how the application's code handles input, so it doesn't depend on an unpatched server. A fully patched server can still host an application vulnerable to XSS.
Incorrect. XSS needs no firewall access beyond the normal access that lets users reach the web application. Loose (promiscuous) firewall rules have no bearing on the attack.

questions.stem: Roger is conducting a software test for a tax preparation application developed by his company. End users will access the application over the web, but Roger is conducting his test on the back end, evaluating the source code on the web server. What type of test is Roger conducting?
questions.explanation: In a white-box test, the tester has access to full implementation details of the system, including source code, prior to beginning the test. In gray-box testing, the tester has partial knowledge. In black-box testing, the tester has no knowledge of the system and tests it from a user perspective. Blue boxes are a phone hacking tool and are not used in software testing.
optionNotes: Correct. Roger is reviewing the source code on the server, so he has full knowledge of how the system is built. That makes this a white-box test.
Incorrect. In gray-box testing the tester has only partial knowledge of the system. Roger has full access to the source code, so this is more than a gray-box test.
Incorrect. A blue box is an old phone-hacking device used to manipulate telephone switching tones. It is not a software testing method.
Incorrect. Black-box testing assumes no knowledge of the system and tests it from the user's side. Roger is examining the back-end source code, so this is not a black-box test.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about heuristic-based antimalware software?
options: It has a lower false positive rate than signature detection.
It requires frequent definition updates to detect new malware.
It has a higher likelihood of detecting zero-day exploits than signature detection.
It monitors systems for files with content known to be viruses.
questions.explanation: Heuristic-based antimalware software has a higher likelihood of detecting a zero-day exploit than signature-based methods. Heuristic-based software does not require frequent signature updates because it does not rely upon monitoring systems for the presence of known malware. The trade-off with this approach is that it has a higher false positive rate than signature detection methods.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Backwards. Heuristic detection flags suspicious behavior instead of exact matches, so it produces more false positives than signature detection. That is the trade-off for catching unknown threats.
Incorrect. Frequent definition updates are what signature-based tools need. Heuristic tools don't depend on lists of known malware, so they don't rely on constant signature updates.
Correct. Heuristics look at behavior and characteristics instead of known signatures, so they can catch zero-day exploits that have no signature yet.
Incorrect. Scanning for content from known viruses describes signature-based detection. Heuristic tools don't depend on known-malware patterns.

questions.stem: Martin is inspecting a system where the user reported unusual activity, including disk activity when the system is idle and abnormal CPU and network usage. He suspects that the machine is infected by a virus, but scans come up clean. What malware technique might be in use here that would explain the clean scan results?
questions.explanation: One possibility for the clean scan results is that the virus is using stealth techniques, such as intercepting read requests from the antivirus software and returning a correct-looking version of the infected file. The system may also be the victim of a zero-day attack, using a virus that is not yet included in the signature definition files provided by the antivirus vendor.
optionNotes: Incorrect. File infector viruses modify executable files, which signature scans normally detect; infecting files doesn't by itself hide the virus from antivirus checks.
Incorrect. MBR viruses describe where the virus lives: they redirect boot to an infected sector. Hiding a clean MBR from antivirus is a stealth technique, not something defined by the MBR type.
Incorrect. Service injection is not a standard virus category, and nothing about it explains how a virus would evade scans.
Correct. Stealth viruses intercept antivirus read requests and return a clean-looking version of the infected file. That explains clean scans despite signs of infection.

questions.stem:
Tomas discovers a line in his application log that appears to correspond with an attempt to conduct a directory traversal attack. He believes the attack was conducted using URL encoding. The line reads as follows: %252E%252E%252F%252E%252E%252Fetc/passwd
What character is represented by the %252E value?
questions.explanation: In URL encoding, the . character is replaced by %252E, and the /character is replaced by %252F. You can see this in the log entry, where the expected pattern of ../../ is replaced by %252E%252E%252F%252E%252E%252F.
optionNotes: Correct. %252E is the double-encoded period (%25 decodes to %, leaving %2E, which is '.'). Together with %252F it rebuilds the ../../ traversal pattern before etc/passwd.
Incorrect. A comma is %2C in URL encoding (%252C double-encoded), not %2E. Commas also have no role in a ../ directory traversal sequence.
Incorrect. A semicolon is %3B (%253B double-encoded). It is used in command injection, not in the ../ path traversal pattern seen in this log.
Incorrect. The forward slash is %252F in this log entry, not %252E. Each %252E%252E%252F group decodes to ../, so the slash is the third value in the group.

questions.stem: An attacker posted a message to a public discussion forum that contains an embedded malicious script that is not displayed to the user but executes on the user's system when read. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: Attacks where the malicious user tricks the victim's web browser into executing a script through the use of a third-party site are known as cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. This particular attack is a persistent XSS attack because it remains on the discussion forum until an administrator discovers and deletes it, giving it the ability to affect many users.
optionNotes: Incorrect. XSRF (CSRF) tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending an unwanted command to another site, like a forged transfer link. Here a script runs on the reader's system, which is XSS, not request forgery.

Incorrect. XSRF is the wrong attack family. CSRF abuses a victim's authenticated session to issue commands to a second site. It is not about a hidden script running in the browser of whoever views a forum post.

Correct. A script hidden in a forum post makes the victim's browser run attacker code through a third-party site, which is XSS. It is persistent because it stays stored on the forum, hitting many visitors until an admin deletes it.

Incorrect. Nonpersistent (reflected) XSS bounces the script off a server in a crafted request or link and is not stored. A forum post that stays on the site and hits every reader is stored, persistent XSS.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a principle of the Agile software development process?
options: Welcome changing requirements, even late in the development process.
Maximizing the amount of work not done is essential.
Clear documentation is the primary measure of progress.
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto includes 12 principles for software development. Three of those are listed as answer choices: maximizing the amount of work not done is essential, build projects around motivated individuals, and welcome changing requirements throughout the development process. Agile does not, however, consider clear documentation the primary measure of progress. Instead, working software is the primary measure of progress.
optionNotes: Incorrect. This is one of the 12 Agile Manifesto principles. Agile welcomes changing requirements even late in development, so it can't be the answer to a 'not a principle' question.
Incorrect. Simplicity, described as the art of maximizing the amount of work not done, is a real Agile principle. That makes it a wrong answer here.
Correct. This is not an Agile principle. Agile treats working software as the primary measure of progress, not documentation, and it values working software over comprehensive documentation.
Incorrect. Building projects around motivated individuals, giving them support and trusting them, is one of the Agile Manifesto principles. So it is a valid principle, not the exception.

questions.stem: Gavin is an internal auditor tasked with examining the change management practices of his organization. He would like to review a series of changes made to a software package to determine whether they were properly documented. Where should he turn for a description of each proposed change?
questions.explanation: Each change should be the result of a reviewed and approved request for change (RFC). These RFCs may be approved by the change advisory board (CAB). The security information and event management (SIEM) and security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platforms used by the organization would not normally contain information about the change management process.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The change advisory board (CAB) is the group that reviews and approves changes. It isn't the document that describes each proposed change; that description lives in the RFC.

Correct. Every change should come from a reviewed and approved request for change (RFC). The RFC documents what the proposed change is, so it's where an auditor would go to check that changes were documented.
Incorrect. SOAR (security orchestration, automation, and response) platforms automate incident response playbooks. They don't normally hold change management records.
Incorrect. A SIEM (security information and event management) system collects and correlates security logs and events. It would not normally contain descriptions of proposed changes.

questions.stem: Neal is working with a DynamoDB database. The database is not structured like a relational database but allows Neal to store data using a key-value store. What type of database is DynamoDB?
questions.explanation: A key-value store is an example of a NoSQL database that does not follow a relational or hierarchical model like traditional databases. A graph database is another example of a NoSQL database, but it uses nodes and edges to store data rather than keys and values.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A relational database stores data in tables of rows and columns linked by keys. The question says DynamoDB is not structured like a relational database.
Incorrect. A graph database is a type of NoSQL database, but it stores data as nodes and edges, not as key-value pairs.
Incorrect. A hierarchical database arranges records in a parent-child tree. That's a traditional model, and key-value stores don't follow it.
Correct. A key-value store like DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, which means it doesn't use the traditional relational or hierarchical models.

questions.stem: In the transaction shown here, what would happen if the database failed in between the first and second update statements? BEGIN TRANSACTION UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 250 WHERE account_number = 1001; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 250 WHERE account_number = 2002; COMMIT TRANSACTION
options: The database would credit the first account with $250 in funds but then not reduce the balance of the second account.
The database would ignore the first command and only reduce the balance of the second account by $250.
The database would roll back the transaction, ignoring the results of both commands.
The database would successfully execute both commands.
questions.explanation: A database failure in the middle of a transaction causes the rollback of the entire transaction. In this scenario, the database would not execute either command because doing so would violate the atomicity property of the transaction.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Crediting account 1001 without debiting 2002 is the partial-completion problem that transactions exist to prevent. Atomicity means the first update can't stand on its own, so $250 can't appear out of thin air.

Incorrect. Skipping the first update while applying the second would also be a partial result, and it would make $250 vanish. Atomicity rules out applying any single statement from a transaction that didn't finish.
Correct. A failure partway through a transaction rolls back the whole transaction, so neither update takes effect. This is the atomicity (all-or-nothing) property of ACID.
Incorrect. The failure happened before the second update and before COMMIT, so the transaction never finished. Neither update is kept, which rules out both commands succeeding.

questions.stem: Tareck's organization makes use of a significant amount of COTS software. He recently discovered a significant buffer overflow vulnerability in the code of a COTS software package that is crucial to his business. What is the most likely way that Tareck can get this corrected?
options: Work with his software development team to modify the code.
Notify the vendor and request a patch.
questions.explanation: When using commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software, customers do not generally have access to the source code and must depend upon the vendor to release security patches that correct vulnerabilities. Other controls, such as intrusion prevention systems and firewalls, may be able to help mitigate the issue, depending upon the nature of the flaw, but they will not correct it.
optionNotes: Incorrect. COTS customers generally don't have the source code, so Tareck's in-house developers can't change the vulnerable code themselves.
Correct. COTS customers rely on the vendor to fix the code. Reporting the buffer overflow and asking for a security patch is how the flaw actually gets fixed.
Incorrect. An IPS might block attempts to exploit the flaw, depending on how it works. That only reduces the risk. The buffer overflow stays in the code.
Incorrect. Changing firewall rules could limit who can reach the vulnerable software. That's a compensating control, and it doesn't remove the flaw.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is true about software testing?
options: Static testing works on runtime environments.
Dynamic testing uses automated tools, but static testing does not.
Static testing is a more important testing technique than dynamic testing.
questions.explanation: Static testing performs code analysis in an offline fashion, without actually executing the code. Dynamic testing evaluates code in a runtime environment. Both static and dynamic testing may use automated tools, and both are important security testing techniques.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Static testing analyzes code offline without executing it. Testing code in a runtime environment is what dynamic testing does.
Correct. Static testing analyzes source or compiled code offline, without running it.
Incorrect. Both static and dynamic testing can use automated tools. Static analyzers that scan code are a common example.
Incorrect. Neither technique is more important. Static and dynamic testing find different problems, and both are important security testing techniques.

questions.stem:
David is working on developing a project schedule for a software development effort, and he comes across the chart shown here. What type of chart is this?
[Figure, described in text: a chart with one row per WBS element (WBS 1 Summary Element 1, WBS 1.1 Activity A … WBS 2.3 Activity G) and horizontal bars drawn against a timeline of weeks, showing each activity's start and end, percent complete, dependencies (start-to-start, finish-to-start, finish-to-finish), and a TODAY line.]
questions.explanation: The chart shown in the figure is a Gantt chart, showing the proposed start and end dates for different activities. It is developed based on the work breakdown structure (WBS), which is developed based on functional requirements. Program Evaluation Review Technique (PERT) charts show the project schedule as a series of numbered nodes.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The work breakdown structure is the input the Gantt chart is built from. A WBS breaks the project into elements, but it doesn't plot those elements as bars against a timeline.
Incorrect. Functional requirements describe what the software has to do, and the WBS is developed from them. They aren't a scheduling chart with timeline bars.
Incorrect. A PERT chart shows the project schedule as a network of numbered nodes. It doesn't use horizontal bars drawn against a calendar timeline.
Correct. A Gantt chart shows each activity's proposed start and end dates as horizontal bars across a timeline. It can also show percent complete and dependencies, which matches the figure.

questions.stem: Barry is a software tester who is working with a new gaming application developed by his company. He is playing the game on a smartphone to conduct his testing in an environment that best simulates a normal end user, but he is referencing the source code as he conducts his test. What type of test is Barry conducting?
questions.explanation: In a gray-box test, the tester evaluates the software from a user perspective but has access to the source code as the test is conducted. White-box tests also have access to the source code but perform testing from a developer's perspective. Black-box tests work from a user's perspective but do not have access to source code. Blue boxes are a telephone hacking tool and not a software testing technique.
optionNotes: Incorrect. White-box testing does give the tester the source code, but the testing is done from a developer's point of view. Barry is testing as a normal end user would, so this isn't white box.
Incorrect. Black-box testing is done from the user's point of view without any access to the source code. Barry has the source code open while he tests, so it can't be black box.
Incorrect. A blue box is an old telephone-hacking device. It isn't a software testing method at all.
Correct. Gray-box testing combines the user's point of view with access to the source code, which is exactly what Barry is doing: playing on a phone like an end user while checking the code.

questions.stem: Miguel recently completed a penetration test of the applications that his organization uses to handle sensitive information. During his testing, he discovered a condition where an attacker can exploit a timing condition to manipulate software into allowing him to perform an unauthorized action. Which one of the following attack types fits this scenario?
questions.explanation: The Time of Check to Time of Use (TOC/TOU) attack exploits timing differences between when a system verifies authorization and software uses that authorization to perform an action. It is an example of a race condition attack. The other three attacks mentioned do not depend on precise timing.
optionNotes: Incorrect. SQL injection puts malicious SQL into input fields so it runs against the back-end database. It's an input-validation flaw, not a timing flaw, so precise timing has nothing to do with it.

Incorrect. Cross-site scripting is a code injection attack that slips attacker script into web pages shown to other users. It doesn't depend on any timing gap between checking authorization and using it.
Incorrect. Pass the hash reuses a stolen password hash to log in without knowing the plaintext password. It's credential theft, not a timing-based race condition.

Correct. TOC/TOU is a race condition. The attacker exploits the gap between when the system checks authorization and when the software acts on it, which matches the timing-based unauthorized action Miguel found.

questions.stem:
What part of the security review process are the input parameters shown in the diagram used for?
[Figure, described in text: Configuration input parameters, User input parameters, Control input parameters and Back-end input parameters all feed into "Parameter tracking through code".]
questions.explanation: Each of these input parameters makes up part of the attack surface of the application. Attackers may opt to target any of them to attack the code or its supporting infrastructure.
optionNotes: Incorrect. SQL injection review only looks at one attack type, where database queries are built from unsanitized input. The diagram tracks every input class (configuration, user, control, back-end) as a possible entry point, not just SQL injection.
Incorrect. A sprint review is an Agile meeting at the end of an iteration where the team demonstrates the work it finished. It isn't a security analysis that traces input parameters through code.

Incorrect. A Fagan inspection is a formal six-step code review process (planning, overview, preparation, inspection, rework, follow-up). It is about the review procedure, not about mapping input parameters.
Correct. Each input parameter shown is part of the application's attack surface, and attackers could target any of them to attack the code or its supporting infrastructure.

questions.stem:
What application security process can be described in these three major steps?
1. Decomposing the application
2. Determining and ranking threats
3. Determining countermeasures and mitigation
questions.explanation: Threat modeling commonly involves decomposing the application to understand it and how it interacts with other components or users. Next, identifying and ranking threats allows you to focus on the threats that should be prioritized. Finally, identifying how to mitigate those threats finishes the process. Once complete, an organization can take action to handle the threats that were identified with appropriate controls.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A Fagan inspection is the most formal type of code review. It has six steps (planning, overview, preparation, inspection, rework, follow-up) and does not decompose an application or rank threats.

Correct. Threat modeling first decomposes the application to see how it interacts with other components and users. It then identifies and ranks threats so the important ones are handled first, and finally works out mitigations.

Incorrect. Penetration testing actively tries to exploit vulnerabilities to check whether security controls work. It is a testing activity, not a process for decomposing an application, ranking threats and planning countermeasures.

Incorrect. Code review means people examine source code to find defects. Its formal version, the Fagan inspection, follows planning, inspection, rework and follow-up steps, not decomposition and threat ranking.

questions.stem: Which one of the following approaches to failure management is the most conservative from a security perspective?
questions.explanation: The fail closed approach prevents any activity from taking place during a system security failure and is the most conservative approach to failure management. Fail open takes the opposite philosophy, allowing all activity in the event of a security control failure. Fail clear and fail mitigation are not failure management approaches.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Fail open is the opposite philosophy. It allows all activity when a security control fails, so it favors availability over security and is the least conservative choice.
Incorrect. "Fail mitigation" isn't a recognized failure management approach. It's a made-up distractor term.
Incorrect. "Fail clear" isn't a recognized failure management approach. It's a made-up term that just sounds plausible.
Correct. Fail closed blocks all activity while a security control is failed, which makes it the most conservative, security-first approach to failure management.

questions.stem:
What software development model is shown here?
[Figure, described in text: a spiral that winds outward through four quadrants: Determine objectives, alternatives, and constraints; Evaluate alternatives, identify and resolve risks; Develop and verify next-level product; Plan next phases. Successive loops pass prototypes P1, P2 and P3.]
questions.explanation: The illustration shows the spiral model of software development. In this approach, developers use multiple iterations of a waterfall-style software development process. This becomes a “loop” of iterations through similar processes. The original waterfall approach does not iterate through the entire process repeatedly. Some variants do allow iteration, but only by allowing movement backward and forward one stage. The Agile approach to software development focuses on iterative improvement and does not follow a rigorous SDLC model. Lean is a process improvement methodology and not a software development model.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Waterfall moves through its stages in order and never repeats the whole process. Some variants let you step back one stage, but none loops through repeated prototypes the way this figure does.
Incorrect. Agile is built on iterative improvement, but it doesn't follow a rigid SDLC structure. So it can't be the picture of formal quadrants with risk analysis and numbered prototypes.
Incorrect. Lean is a process improvement method, not a software development model, so it can't be what the figure shows.

Correct. The spiral model runs the waterfall-style process many times as repeated loops. Each loop sets objectives, analyzes risk, develops a product and plans the next phase, producing prototypes P1, P2 and P3.

questions.stem: Mark is considering replacing his organization's customer relationship management (CRM) solution with a new product that is available in the cloud. This new solution is completely managed by the vendor, and Mark's company will not have to write any code or manage any physical resources. What type of cloud solution is Mark considering?
questions.explanation: In a software-as-a-service solution, the vendor manages both the physical infrastructure and the complete application stack, providing the customer with access to a fully managed application.
optionNotes: Incorrect. With Infrastructure as a Service, the vendor supplies only the virtualized compute, storage and network. The customer still manages the OS, applications and code, so it isn't a fully vendor-managed CRM.

Incorrect. Containers as a Service hosts and orchestrates the customer's own containerized workloads. The customer still builds and manages the application code inside the containers, which Mark's company won't have to do.
Incorrect. With Platform as a Service, the provider manages the hardware and runtime platform, but the customer writes and deploys its own application code. Mark's company won't write any code.

Correct. With SaaS, the vendor manages both the physical infrastructure and the whole application stack, and the customer just uses a fully managed application. That matches a vendor-managed cloud CRM.

questions.stem: Which one of the following change management processes is initiated by users rather than developers?
questions.explanation: The request process begins with a user-initiated request for a feature. Change and release control are initiated by developers seeking to implement changes. Design review is a phase of the change approval process initiated by developers when they have a completed design.
optionNotes: Correct. The request process starts when a user asks for a new feature or modification, so it's the one change management process that users rather than developers kick off.
Incorrect. Change control is started by developers who want to implement changes in a controlled, approved way. Users don't initiate it.
Incorrect. Release control is driven by developers. It covers approving and deploying finished changes into production, not users asking for features.
Incorrect. Design review is a step in the change approval process. Developers start it once they have a completed design.

questions.stem: Teagan would like to better protect his organization against database inference attacks. Which one of the following techniques is an effective countermeasure against these attacks?
questions.explanation: Polyinstantiation allows the storage of multiple different pieces of information in a database at different classification levels to prevent attackers from inferring anything about the absence of information. Input validation, server-side validation, and parameterization are all techniques used to prevent web application attacks and are not effective against inference attacks.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Input validation filters user-supplied data to stop web application attacks such as SQL injection and XSS. It does nothing to stop users from inferring sensitive facts out of data they're allowed to see.

Incorrect. Parameterization (prepared statements) keeps user input from changing how a SQL query runs, which defends against injection. It can't stop users from drawing inferences from legitimate query results.
Correct. Polyinstantiation stores different versions of a record at different classification levels. Lower-cleared users can't learn anything from missing or hidden data, which blocks inference.
Incorrect. Server-side validation checks input on the server so a client can't bypass the checks. Like other web application controls, it doesn't address inference attacks.

questions.stem: Ursula is a government web developer who recently created a public application that offers property records. She would like to make it available for other developers to integrate into their applications. What can Ursula create to make it easiest for developers to call her code directly and integrate the output into their applications?
questions.explanation: While Ursula may certainly use an object model, data dictionary, and primary key in her development effort, external developers cannot directly use them to access her code. An application programming interface (API) allows other developers to call Ursula's code from within their own without knowing the details of Ursula's implementation.
optionNotes: Incorrect. An object model describes how objects and classes in Ursula's code are structured. It's an internal design tool, so outside developers can't use it to call her code.
Incorrect. A data dictionary is the central catalog of data elements and their definitions inside a database. It documents her data but gives outside developers no way to call her code.
Correct. An API exposes defined calls that let other developers call Ursula's code from inside their own applications. They don't need to know how she implemented it.
Incorrect. A primary key is the attribute that uniquely identifies each row in a database table. It's an internal database element, not an interface outside developers can call.

questions.stem: Nathan recently completed a software development project where he integrated the organization's network operations stack with their development processes. As a result, developers can modify firewall rules from their code on an as-needed basis. What term best describes this ability?
questions.explanation: This is an example of software-defined security (SDS), where security infrastructure may be easily manipulated by code. Answering this question is tricky because several of the other terms are closely related. Software-defined security is an example of infrastructure as code (IaC), but SDS is a more descriptive, and therefore better, answer. SDS is commonly used within an Agile development framework. The DevOps approach links together development and operations but is generally called DevSecOps when it also includes SDS.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Agile is an iterative software development methodology. SDS is often used inside Agile teams, but Agile doesn't describe changing firewall rules through code.

Incorrect. Infrastructure as code is the broader category, and SDS is one example of it. Because the question is specifically about security controls like firewall rules, SDS is the more precise and therefore better answer.
Correct. Software-defined security (SDS) means security infrastructure, such as firewall rules, can be changed directly through code as needed. That is exactly the ability described.
Incorrect. DevOps joins development and operations, but on its own it doesn't describe security controls changed by code. When the approach also includes SDS, it is usually called DevSecOps.

questions.stem:
TJ is inspecting a system where the user reported a strange error message and the inability to access files. He sees the window shown here. What type of malware should TJ suspect?
[Figure, described in text: a CryptoLocker window headed "Your personal files are encrypted!" It says the user's files were encrypted with a unique RSA-2048 public key, that the only copy of the private key is on a secret server and will be destroyed after a deadline (a countdown shows 57:45:37), and that the user must pay 300 USD / 300 EUR to obtain the private key; a "Next >>" button leads to payment.]
questions.explanation: Messages similar to the one shown here are indicative of a ransomware attack. The attacker encrypts files on a user's hard drive and then demands a ransom, normally paid in Bitcoin, for the decryption key required to restore access to the original content. Encrypted viruses, on the other hand, use encryption to hide themselves from antivirus mechanisms and do not alter other contents on the system.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Service injection is a way of hiding malicious code inside a legitimate system service or process. It doesn't encrypt the user's files or show a payment demand, which is what this window does.
Incorrect. An encrypted virus encrypts its own code to avoid antivirus detection. It doesn't change other content on the system, so it wouldn't lock the user's files or demand money.
Incorrect. SQL injection attacks a web application's database by inserting malicious queries. It doesn't infect an endpoint, encrypt local files, or display a ransom countdown.

Correct. Ransomware encrypts the user's files with a key only the attacker holds, then demands payment for the decryption key. The CryptoLocker message, with its deadline and $300 demand, is a classic example.

questions.stem: Charles is developing a mission-critical application that has a direct impact on human safety. Time and cost are less important than correctly functioning software. Which of the following software development methodologies should he choose given these requirements?
questions.explanation: Despite many organizations moving to Agile, DevOps, or other more responsive development methodologies, waterfall remains a strong contender when clear objectives and stable requirements are combined with a need to prevent flaws and to have a high level of control over the development process and output.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Agile puts speed, frequent delivery and changing requirements first. This mission-critical, safety-related project needs stable requirements and tight control to prevent flaws, so Agile is the weaker fit.
Incorrect. DevOps combines development and operations to deploy quickly and continuously. Fast, frequent change doesn't match a project that values correctness and control over time and cost.

Incorrect. Spiral is a risk-driven iterative model that repeats its phases in cycles. It's useful when requirements are evolving, but it gives less of the linear, tightly controlled process that waterfall offers for stable, safety-critical requirements.

Correct. Waterfall fits best when objectives are clear and requirements are stable, and when the priority is preventing flaws and keeping a high level of control over the development process and its output.

questions.stem: Which one of the following types of artificial intelligence attempts to use complex computations to replicate the partial function of the human mind?
questions.explanation: Neural networks attempt to use complex computational techniques to model the behavior of the human mind. Knowledge banks are a component of expert systems, which are designed to capture and reapply human knowledge. Decision support systems are designed to provide advice to those carrying out standard procedures and are often driven by expert systems.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Decision support systems give advice to people carrying out standard procedures and are often driven by expert systems. They don't computationally model how the human mind works.
Incorrect. Expert systems capture human expert knowledge as if/then rules and apply it again later. They don't use complex computations to replicate how the mind works.
Incorrect. A knowledge bank (knowledge base) is the rule store inside an expert system, not a separate type of AI. It does not model human thinking.
Correct. Neural networks use layers of weighted computations to model part of how the human brain works.

questions.stem: At which level of the Software Capability Maturity Model (SW-CMM) does an organization introduce basic life-cycle management processes?
questions.explanation: In level 2, the Repeatable level of the SW-CMM, an organization introduces basic life cycle management processes. Reuse of code in an organized fashion begins, and repeatable results are expected from similar projects. The key process areas for this level include Requirements Management, Software Project Planning, Software Project Tracking and Oversight, Software Subcontract Management, Software Quality Assurance, and Software Configuration Management.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Level 1, Initial, is where work is ad hoc and chaotic with no formal process at all. Basic life-cycle management only appears at the next level.

Correct. Level 2, Repeatable, brings in basic life-cycle management, organized code reuse and repeatable results on similar projects. Its key process areas include requirements management, project planning and configuration management.
Incorrect. Level 3, Defined, comes after Repeatable. Here the organization runs formal, documented standard processes. It goes beyond introducing basic life-cycle management.
Incorrect. Level 4, Managed, uses quantitative measures to understand and control the development process. That is much more mature than first introducing basic life-cycle processes.

questions.stem: Lucas runs the accounting systems for his company. The morning after an essential employee was fired, systems began mysteriously losing information. Lucas suspects that the fired employee tampered with the systems prior to his departure. What type of attack should Lucas suspect?
questions.explanation: The critical fact in this question is that Lucas suspects the tampering took place before the employee departed. This is the signature of a logic bomb: malicious code that lies dormant until certain conditions are met. The other attack types listed here—privilege escalation, SQL injection, and remote code execution—would more likely take place in real time.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Privilege escalation means gaining higher rights than you were granted. It happens while the attacker is actively working, not as dormant code planted before someone leaves.
Incorrect. SQL injection sends malicious input to a database-backed application while the attack is underway. It isn't code planted ahead of time that waits to go off after the employee has left.
Correct. A logic bomb is malicious code that sits dormant until a condition is met, such as the employee's termination. That fits tampering done before he left that only showed up the next morning.

Incorrect. Remote code execution means an attacker runs commands on a target from a distance while the attack is happening. It doesn't explain damage set up in advance by an insider who has since left.

questions.stem: Which one of the following principles would not be favored in an Agile approach to software development?
options: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
Responding to change over following a plan
questions.explanation: The Agile approach to software development embraces four principles. It values individuals and interactions over processes and tools, working software over comprehensive documentation, customer collaboration over contract negotiation, and responding to change over following a plan.
optionNotes: Correct. This turns the Agile Manifesto around: Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools, so this principle would not be favored.
Incorrect. This is one of the four Agile Manifesto values. Agile puts working software ahead of comprehensive documentation.
Incorrect. This is a real Agile value. Agile prefers ongoing customer collaboration to rigid contract negotiation.
Incorrect. This is a real Agile value. Agile prefers adapting to change over sticking to a fixed plan, which sets it apart from waterfall.

questions.stem: What technique do API developers most commonly use to limit access to an API to authorized individuals and applications?
questions.explanation: API developers commonly use API keys to limit access to authorized users and applications. Encryption provides for confidentiality of information exchanged using an API but does not provide authentication. Input validation is an application security technique used to protect against malicious input. IP filters may be used to limit access to an API, but they are not commonly used because it is difficult to deploy an API with IP filters since the filters require constant modification and maintenance as endpoints change.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Encryption keeps data exchanged through the API confidential, but it doesn't authenticate anyone, so it can't limit access to authorized users or apps.
Incorrect. Input validation protects the application from malicious input. It is not a way to identify or authorize the caller.
Correct. API keys are the most common way developers restrict an API to authorized users and applications. Each caller sends a key that identifies it and is checked before access is granted.
Incorrect. IP filters can restrict API access, but they are not commonly used. They need constant updating and maintenance as endpoints change, which makes them hard to deploy.

questions.stem: Reggie recently received a letter from his company's internal auditors scheduling the kickoff meeting for an assessment of his group. Which of the following should Reggie not expect to learn during that meeting?
questions.explanation: An audit kickoff meeting should clearly describe the scope and purpose of the audit as well as the expected time frame. Auditors should never approach an audit with any expectations about what they will discover because the findings should be developed based only upon the results of audit examinations.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The kickoff meeting should spell out the audit's scope, meaning which systems, processes and groups will be examined. Reggie should expect to hear this, so it is not the answer.
Incorrect. Explaining why the audit is being done (its purpose) is a standard part of the kickoff meeting. Reggie should expect to learn it, so this is not the answer.
Incorrect. Auditors normally share the expected timeframe at kickoff so the audited group can plan resources and availability. Reggie should expect this information.
Correct. Auditors should not go into an audit expecting particular findings. Findings come only from the results of the audit examinations, so they can't be presented at the kickoff meeting.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the proper order of steps in the waterfall model of software development?
questions.explanation: In the waterfall model, the software development process follows five sequential steps that are, in order, Requirements, Design, Coding, Testing, and Maintenance. Note that these phases may be further subdivided. The Requirements phase often begins with System Requirements and then moves on to Software Requirements. The Design phase often begins with Preliminary Design and then moves on to Detailed Design.
optionNotes: Incorrect. This option puts Testing before Coding. Code has to exist before it can be tested, so in the waterfall model Coding comes right after Design and Testing follows it.

Correct. The waterfall model runs through five steps in order: Requirements, Design, Coding, Testing, Maintenance. Requirements and Design can each be split further, for example System/Software Requirements and Preliminary/Detailed Design.

Incorrect. This option puts Design before Requirements. In the waterfall model, requirements are gathered first so that the design is based on them, starting with system requirements and then software requirements.
Incorrect. This option gets two pairs backwards: Design comes before Requirements and Testing comes before Coding. Waterfall goes Requirements, Design, Coding, Testing, then Maintenance.

questions.stem: Renee is a software developer who writes code in Node.js for her organization. The company is considering moving from a self-hosted Node.js environment to one where Renee will run her code on application servers managed by a cloud vendor. What type of cloud solution is Renee's company considering?
questions.explanation: In a platform-as-a-service solution, the customer supplies application code that the vendor then executes on its own infrastructure.
optionNotes: Incorrect. With IaaS the vendor supplies only raw compute, storage, and networking. Renee's company would still have to manage the OS and the Node.js runtime itself, but the question says the vendor manages the application servers.

Incorrect. CaaS (containers as a service) hosts containers: packages that bundle an application with everything it needs to run. Here Renee hands over plain code to run on the vendor's managed application servers, not container images.
Correct. In PaaS the customer supplies the application code, such as Renee's Node.js code, and the vendor runs it on infrastructure and application servers that the vendor manages.
Incorrect. SaaS gives customers a finished application built by the vendor. Customers don't write or deploy their own code, so it doesn't fit a developer running her own Node.js code.

questions.stem: Tom is writing a software program that calculates the sales tax for online orders placed from various jurisdictions. The application includes a user-defined field that allows the entry of the total sale amount. Tom would like to ensure that the data entered in this field is a properly formatted dollar amount. What technique should he use?
questions.explanation: Input validation ensures that the data provided to a program as input matches the expected parameters. Limit checks are a special form of input validation that ensure that the value remains within an expected range, but there was no range specified in this scenario. Fail open and fail secure are options when planning for possible system failures.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A limit check is a kind of input validation that makes sure a value falls within an expected range. The scenario asks about format, not a range, so this is too narrow.
Incorrect. Fail open describes how a system behaves when it fails: it allows access or keeps working. It has nothing to do with checking whether a dollar amount is formatted correctly.
Incorrect. Fail secure is a failure-handling choice where the system locks down when it fails. It doesn't check user input for the correct format.
Correct. Input validation checks that the data given to a program matches the expected parameters. That includes making sure a field holds a properly formatted dollar amount.

questions.stem: Brian is helping implement a new software testing methodology for his organization and would like to review the completeness of his toolkit. Which of the following would be considered dynamic application security testing (DAST) tools? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Dynamic application security tools conduct their testing by actually executing the code. This is the case for both fuzzing and web application vulnerability scanning. Code reviews and static analysis packages analyze the code itself but do not execute it, making them static application security testing (SAST) tools.
optionNotes: Incorrect. In a code review, people read the source code without running it. That makes it a static (SAST) technique, not a DAST one.
Correct. Fuzzing runs the program and feeds it random or malformed input to see whether it crashes or misbehaves. Because the code is executed, it counts as dynamic testing (DAST).
Incorrect. Static analysis tools examine source code or compiled binaries without executing them, so they are SAST tools by definition.
Correct. A web application vulnerability scanner probes the running application with live requests. Testing the code while it executes makes this a DAST tool.

questions.stem:
What approach to technology management integrates the three components of technology management shown in this illustration?
[Figure, described in text: a Venn diagram of three overlapping circles labeled Software Development, Quality Assurance and Operations.]
questions.explanation: The DevOps approach to technology management seeks to integrate software development, operations, and quality assurance in a seamless approach that builds collaboration between the three disciplines.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Agile is an iterative software development methodology built on the Agile Manifesto. It deals with how software gets built, not with merging development, QA and operations into one operating model.
Incorrect. Lean is a process-improvement philosophy about cutting waste and adding value. It is not the approach that joins development, operations and quality assurance into one model.
Correct. DevOps brings software development, operations and quality assurance together into one collaborative model. That matches the three overlapping circles in the diagram.
Incorrect. ITIL is a framework of best practices for IT service management. It does not specifically aim to merge development, QA and operations the way DevOps does.

questions.stem: Olivia is conducting a risk analysis of a web application that her organization obtained from a third party and is concerned that it might contain vulnerabilities. Which one of the following activities might she take to best mitigate the risk?
questions.explanation: Deploying a web application firewall (WAF) may reduce the likelihood or impact of a web application vulnerability and is, therefore, a good example of risk mitigation. Encryption is also a risk mitigation control, but it is less likely be effective against a web application security flaw. Purchasing an insurance policy is an example of risk transference, not risk mitigation. Discontinuing use of the software is an example of risk avoidance, not risk mitigation.
optionNotes: Correct. A WAF filters malicious web traffic such as injection and XSS attempts. That lowers the chance or impact of exploiting flaws in the third-party app, which makes it a direct form of risk mitigation.
Incorrect. Encryption is a mitigation control, but it protects data confidentiality. It does little to stop attacks that exploit web application code flaws, so it is a weaker fit than a WAF.
Incorrect. Buying insurance moves the financial impact to another party. That is risk transference, not mitigation, and it does nothing to reduce the vulnerabilities themselves.
Incorrect. Stopping use of the software removes the risk entirely. That is risk avoidance, not mitigation of a risk the organization keeps.

questions.stem: Which one of the following database concurrency issues occurs when one transaction reads information that was written to a database by a second transaction that never committed?
questions.explanation: Dirty reads occur when one transaction reads a value from a database that was written by another transaction that did not commit. Lost updates occur when one transaction writes a value to the database that overwrites a value needed by transactions that have earlier precedence, causing those transactions to read an incorrect value. Incorrect summaries occur when one transaction is using an aggregate function to summarize data stored in a database, while a second transaction is making modifications to the database, causing the summary to include incorrect information. SQL injection is a web application security flaw, not a database concurrency problem.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A lost update happens when one transaction's write overwrites a value that earlier transactions still needed, so those transactions end up with wrong data. The problem is with overlapping writes, not with reading data that was never committed.
Incorrect. SQL injection is a security flaw in web applications that lets an attacker insert malicious SQL. It is an attack, not a concurrency problem between transactions.
Incorrect. An incorrect summary happens when an aggregate function runs while another transaction is changing the data, so the result is inaccurate. It is not about reading uncommitted writes.
Correct. A dirty read is when one transaction reads a value written by another transaction that never committed, so the value it read may later be rolled back.

questions.stem: What software development concept was pioneered by the Defense Department in the 1990s as an effort to bring together diverse product development teams?
questions.explanation: The integrated product team (IPT) approach brought together cross-functional teams and was designed by the U.S. Department of Defense in 1995. It was a predecessor to the Agile methodology, which uses tools like the scrum approach and user stories to conduct software development work.
optionNotes: Correct. The U.S. Department of Defense introduced the integrated product team (IPT) in 1995 to pull cross-functional teams together on product development.
Incorrect. Agile came after IPT and grew out of the software industry (Agile Manifesto, 2001), not out of the DoD. IPT was one of its predecessors.
Incorrect. Scrum is a framework that Agile teams use to organize work in sprints. It is not the DoD's 1990s cross-team initiative.
Incorrect. User stories are an Agile tool for writing requirements from the user's point of view. They are not a DoD team-integration concept.

questions.stem: Frank is working to select a new cloud service that will provide block storage for a server being built by his team. What category of cloud service is Frank planning to use?
questions.explanation: Storage is an infrastructure component and, therefore, a block storage service is an example of an infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) cloud service. Software-as-a-service (SaaS) models provide full applications managed by the provider. Platform-as-a-service (PaaS) and function-as-a-service (FaaS) approaches allow developers to run their own code on an infrastructure platform managed by the provider.
optionNotes: Incorrect. SaaS delivers complete applications that the provider manages. Frank needs raw block storage for a server, not a finished application.
Correct. Block storage is an infrastructure component, the same kind of thing as compute and networking, so a block storage service falls under infrastructure as a service (IaaS).
Incorrect. FaaS lets developers run individual functions of their own code on a platform the provider manages. It doesn't supply block storage volumes for a server.
Incorrect. PaaS gives developers a provider-managed platform for running their own code. It hides the underlying infrastructure, such as block storage, rather than providing it directly.

questions.stem:
Match the numbered code testing methods to their lettered definition:
Code testing methods:
1. Regression testing
2. Integration testing
3. Unit testing
4. System testing

(Arrange the options in the order of the numbered items 1–4.)
options: Testing on a complete integrated product
A testing method that focuses on modules or smaller sections of code for testing
A testing method that is used to verify that previously tested software performs the same way after changes are made
A testing method used to validate how software modules work together
questions.explanation:
The code testing methods match to their definitions as follows:
1. Regression testing: C. A testing method that is used to verify that previously tested software performs the same way after changes are made
2. Integration testing: D. A testing method used to validate how software modules work together
3. Unit testing: B. A testing method that focuses on modules or smaller sections of code for testing
4. System testing: A. Testing on a complete integrated product
optionNotes: Goes with item 4, system testing. That method tests the complete, integrated product as a whole, not individual modules or the links between them.
Goes with item 3, unit testing. Unit testing checks individual modules or small sections of code in isolation, before they are combined.
Goes with item 1, regression testing. Regression testing re-checks software that already passed testing to confirm it still behaves the same way after changes are made.
Goes with item 2, integration testing. Integration testing checks how separately tested modules work together and how they interface with each other.

questions.stem:
Match the following numbered terms to their lettered definitions:
1. Session hijacking
2. Cross-site scripting
3. Cross-site request forgery
4. SQL injection

(Arrange the options in the order of the numbered items 1–4.)
options: An attack that injects a malicious script into otherwise trusted websites
An attack that is designed to execute commands against a database via an insecure web application
An exploitation method that often involves cookies or keys to gain unauthorized access to a computer or service
An attack that forces a user to execute unwanted actions in a website or application they are currently logged into
questions.explanation:
The terms match to their definitions as follows:
1. Session hijacking: C. An exploitation method that often involves cookies or keys to gain unauthorized access to a computer or service
2. Cross-site scripting: A. An attack that injects a malicious script into otherwise trusted websites
3. Cross-site request forgery: D. An attack that forces a user to execute unwanted actions in a website or application they are currently logged into
4. SQL injection: B. An attack that is designed to execute commands against a database via an insecure web application
optionNotes: Belongs to item 2, cross-site scripting: the attacker plants a malicious script in a trusted website, and it runs in the browsers of visitors who trust that site.
Belongs to item 4, SQL injection: input that the web application doesn't validate properly is passed to the backend database and run as SQL commands.
Belongs to item 1, session hijacking: the attacker steals or reuses session cookies or keys to take over a session that is already authenticated, gaining unauthorized access.
Belongs to item 3, cross-site request forgery: it exploits the trust a site places in a user who is already logged in, causing their browser to send actions the user never intended.
